decisions.decision: Excluded apps/v4/registry/_legacy-base-colors.ts (1,113 decls), apps/v4/registry/_legacy-colors.ts (1,200 decls), apps/v4/registry/themes.ts (840 decls) and apps/v4/app/legacy-themes.css (439 decls) from the declared token system.
decisions.moved: run.token_count from a raw discovery figure of 1,185 concepts down to 40 canonical tokens; single-source, coverage and orphans all graded against the smaller, real system instead of being swamped by catalog data.
decisions.other_reading: All four files are reachable from owned production entry points and declaration-shaped, so a stricter reading of 'discover every candidate, prove it ships' would inventory them as canonical sources the same as globals.css.

decisions.decision: Reported a deduplicated, collapsed canonical token count (40) as run.token_count, not the raw discover_tokens.py concept count for globals.css (93) or the theoretical alias_of-is-null count (35).
decisions.moved: The headline count away from double-counting Tailwind v4's own '@theme inline' pattern: 53 of the 93 raw concepts are same-file CSS-custom-property aliases (e.g. concept 'primary' and concept 'color-primary', the latter's sole value being 'var(--primary)') that discover_tokens.py's projection-collapse rule does not yet fold into their canonical concept — that rule currently covers only SCSS-to-CSS-custom-property compilation. This run applied that collapse by hand for tokens.filtered.json, merging each alias's site onto its canonical concept as a 'projected_from' entry. chart-1..5 (family 'color') were kept as their own canonical concepts rather than collapsed, because their alias target (--color-blue-300..800) is Tailwind's own default palette, not a name declared in this file — references/vitals.md's framework-default rule counts a project's own reference to a framework default as the project's token. font-sans/font-heading/font-mono were excluded rather than counted, because their @theme-inline declaration is self-referential (alias_of == its own id) — a passthrough for a next/font runtime-injected value, not a static definition.
decisions.other_reading: A stricter, literal reading of the tool's own concept list would report 93 (no collapsing) or 35 (collapsing only alias_of-is-null concepts, which would incorrectly also drop chart-1..5).

decisions.decision: Excluded 20 'canonical' concepts discover_tokens.py found outside globals.css (apps/v4/lib/font-definitions.ts, hooks/use-meta-color.ts, app/layout.tsx, app/(view)/preview/typeset/layout.tsx, and several font-loader helper files) from the token count.
decisions.moved: token_count away from counting non-token JS object properties as design tokens, and stack.token_sources down to the one file the project actually declares its design tokens in.
decisions.other_reading: Inspecting each: 'opengraph.width'/'opengraph.height' are literal OpenGraph image pixel dimensions (app/layout.tsx:45-46), 'icons.icon' is a favicon file path (app/layout.tsx:59), 'meta-theme-colors.dark'/'meta-theme-colors.light' are PWA theme-color meta values (hooks/use-meta-color.ts:5-6), and the rest (label/name/title/variable/registryvariable/previewvariable/value) are internal property names inside a custom font-loader's metadata records (lib/font-definitions.ts) — none is a name a component author would type in place of a value. The conservative-js-theme-object extractor currently has no shape heuristic to tell a real token map from an arbitrary data object; this is a tool limitation worth fixing, not a project finding.

decisions.decision: Graded leakage 'pass' rather than 'attention', though a real uncovered finding exists (#000000 x 24 in packages/shadcn/src/tailwind.css) and a large pool of literals (214 bracket-arbitrary px/rem values, near-miss overall) is unreviewed.
decisions.moved: The mechanical grade follows references/vitals.md's stated rule exactly: leakage's pass/attention/fail line reads only the redundant tier, and audit_literal_colors.py found zero redundant and zero exact-value-candidate findings across the 13 consumer stylesheets it scanned.
decisions.other_reading: A reader could reasonably want 'attention' here so the grade itself flags that something is unresolved, rather than relying on this note and the uncovered-tier listing to carry that signal — near-miss stayed unmeasured for color, and Tailwind bracket-arbitrary literals in .tsx (where the shimmer-color-[#378ADD] finding and the 214 unreviewed dimension literals both live) are outside what audit_literal_colors.py scans at all.

decisions.decision: Graded mode-completeness from an agent reading apps/v4/app/globals.css's :root (line 99) and .dark (line 143) blocks directly, side by side, rather than from a tool-verified compiled or runtime artifact.
decisions.moved: mode-completeness to 'pass' with real file:line evidence, instead of 'blocked' — discovery.mode_resolution's own capability stayed unmeasured (the generic engine has no CSS-source-pairing check, only a build/runtime-artifact one), so a strict reading of the vitals.md instruction ('graded only where compiled or resolved output exists') would leave this blocked.
decisions.other_reading: references/vitals.md's mode-completeness signal is stated as 'the set difference across mode blocks' without requiring compiled output specifically (unlike coverage's framework-default rule, which is explicit about needing a checked version) — reading source blocks directly is a legitimate way to compute that set difference, and the original run against this same repository did the same thing.

tier-integrity.note: 10 of 485 .tsx files in registry/new-york-v4 (2.1%) use a raw Tailwind palette utility (blue-500, red-600, neutral-200, and similar) where a semantic token already covers the case — every one of them inside registry/new-york-v4/examples/*, files that intentionally demo arbitrary colors (a spinner in five colors, password-strength indicators, toggle/checkbox color variants), not core chrome. 2.1% falls in the >0%-to-5% attention band. registry/new-york-v4/ui/bubble.tsx:29 was checked and excluded — its bg-[oklch(from_var(--primary)_...)] values derive from var(--primary), which references/adapters/tailwind.md says clears the bar; only bare literals count.

leakage.note: audit_literal_colors.py scanned 13 owned reachable consumer stylesheets and found zero redundant and zero exact-value-candidate findings; leakage's pass/attention/fail line reads only the redundant tier (references/vitals.md), so the mechanical grade is pass. Two real uncovered findings still exist (not in fix_queue — an uncovered finding has no replacement token to queue): #000000 x24 in the CLI's shipped packages/shadcn/src/tailwind.css, and #378ADD x3 (one literal, three near-identical demo files) in a Tailwind bracket-arbitrary class the generic scanner does not check (registry/new-york-v4/examples/{aria,base,radix}/shimmer-color.tsx:7). near-miss stayed unmeasured for color, and 214 further Tailwind bracket-arbitrary px/rem literals across registry/new-york-v4 were found but not individually reviewed — see decisions.

coverage.note: 9 of 11 categories present. color, typography, space, size, radius, border, elevation, motion and breakpoint all resolve to a real token — either a project token in globals.css, or one of Tailwind v4's own default-theme tokens the project imports and never overrides (verified against tailwindcss@4.3.0, the exact version pinned in pnpm-lock.yaml). z-index and opacity do not: Tailwind v4 ships no --z-* or --opacity-* default theme scale, so z-50 and opacity-50 compile to fixed values with nothing for a component author to reach for instead. 9/11 falls in the 8-10 attention band.

mode-completeness.note: Every color-family token declared in :root (light, starting line 99) is redefined in .dark (starting line 143): background, foreground, card, popover, primary, secondary, muted, accent, destructive, border, input, ring, chart-1..5, all 8 sidebar tokens, surface, code/code-foreground, code-highlight, code-number, selection, selection-foreground — zero gaps. The one property in :root absent from .dark is --radius (globals.css:100), a corner-radius value; .dark applies as an additional class alongside :root rather than replacing it, and references/vitals.md scopes mode-completeness to appearance-dependent tokens, putting geometry out of scope by default — the same judgment call the original run made. chart-1..5 resolve to the identical Tailwind-default value in both blocks, so the chart palette itself does not shift with the mode; that is a deliberate constant, not a gap. This grade comes from an agent reading both CSS blocks directly, not from a tool-verified compiled artifact — discovery.mode_resolution's own capability stayed unmeasured — see decisions.

naming-coherence.note: Every one of the 40 canonical tokens and the same-file aliases/projections that build on them follows one grammar: a kebab-case role name, optionally suffixed -foreground for the paired on-color text (accent/accent-foreground, sidebar-accent/sidebar-accent-foreground, and so on). No second grammar or legacy family found within the declared scope.

single-source.note: Within the declared scope (globals.css), every one of the 40 canonical concepts has exactly one definition site. apps/v4/registry/themes.ts and apps/v4/app/legacy-themes.css do redeclare the same names (chart-1..5 and others) with alternate values, but those are the theme-gallery/legacy-preview catalog this run scoped out as content rather than the site's own applied system — see decisions[0]. That exclusion is what changed this grade from the original run's attention.

orphans.note: Checked all 55 declared token names (40 canonical + the remaining same-file aliases not folded into a parent, such as the individual @theme-inline color-* projection names) for at least one reference in apps/v4, combining two search forms: a Tailwind-utility-class grep (bg-x, text-x, border-x, and so on) across registry/new-york-v4, components, app, examples, hooks and lib, and a direct var(--x)/pseudo-selector grep against every reachable file including globals.css itself. The utility-class search alone showed 4 apparent zero-hit names — code-highlight, code-number, selection, selection-foreground — and all four turned out to be used, just not via a Tailwind class: selection/selection-foreground back the ::selection rule at globals.css:195, and code-highlight/code-number are consumed via direct var(--color-code-highlight)/var(--color-code-number) CSS at globals.css:365,372,426 (rehype-pretty-code line-highlighting). No orphaned token found.

enforcement.note: No lint rule or CI gate in this repository reads the token layer. apps/v4/eslint.config.mjs runs eslint-config-next plus typescript-eslint scoped to type-import style and React hooks correctness — nothing about colors, spacing, or bracket-arbitrary literals. No stylelint config exists anywhere in the repository. .github/workflows/code-check.yml runs pnpm lint / format:check / typecheck; .github/workflows/monitor-registries.yml checks registry health (broken imports, stale exports), not token usage. 0 qualifying rules found, so per the vital's own grading this is blocked rather than failed.
